title: Ishtkar Ali v. State of U.P.
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Anish Kumar Gupta, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Para 6.5 objection
headnote: On a preliminary objection that Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a remedy to dispute or correct an electricity bill, the Division Bench disposed of the writ without examining merits and granted liberty to file a clause 6.5 objection before respondent No. 4 within four weeks, to be decided within the next four weeks after hearing.
facts: Ishtkar Ali filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and others, including the distribution licensee, concerning an electricity bill. Counsel for the licensee (respondents 2 to 4) objected that the petition was not maintainable because Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provided a remedy to raise all disputes regarding the bill or to seek its correction. Counsel for the petitioner, the State, and the licensee were heard.

holding_units.topic: billing dispute — alternate remedy under clause 6.5
holding_units.holding: A writ raising a dispute regarding an electricity bill or seeking its correction is disposed of without opinion on merits where Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a remedy. The consumer was given liberty to submit an objection under Para 6.5 before respondent No. 4 within four weeks; if so submitted, it shall be decided in accordance with law within the next four weeks after a reasonable opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: The Court accepted the licensee's maintainability objection and disposed of the writ by relegating the consumer to a Para 6.5 objection instead of examining the bill on the writ side.
Para 6.5 was treated as the statutory forum for all disputes regarding the electricity bill or its correction.

not_decided.point: merits of the petitioner's billing dispute
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on merits; respondent No. 4 is to decide the clause 6.5 objection in accordance with law.
